newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Exchange looking at "unusual" Thursday opening.
newsitem.headline: HK Exchange looking at "unusual" Thursday opening.

text.p: The Stock Exchange of Hong Kong is looking into unusual trading activity at the open of the Thursday morning session, a senior stock exchange official said.

"We are examining the opening transactions in a number of stocks and going to the brokers involved in those transactions and asking them to explain what took place," said Paul Phenix, executive director of the exchange's compliance division.
The Hang Seng Index surged 213 points to an all-time high of 13,744.30 in the first 15 minutes but closed the morning 31.57 points down at 13,499.38, off a session low of 13,424.43.
Brokers said the leap was not derived solely from overnight trading in London, where the Hang Seng London Reference Index put on 46.28 points to close at 13,577.23.
Brokers said there appeared to be massive programme trading at the open, possibly related to the expiry of November index futures later on Thursday.
The unusually large price swing may point to a programme that did not run properly, a market source said.
Phenix said the stock exchange's surveillance system is set up to scrutinise any odd trades during the course of the day as well as those at the opening and close.
